rows: Mexico: The Good Earth
Gordon C. Abbott photographed fields and farmland in Mexico in 1925. The picture shows how people worked the land, with hills in the distance.
What crops do you think grew here?
Jewish Grandmother, Ellis Island
Lewis Hine photographed an elderly Jewish immigrant woman at Ellis Island, where millions of newcomers entered America. Hine's portraits showed the dignity of people arriving with little.
What do you think she was feeling?
USS Constellation, Newport, 1926
Underwood and Underwood photographed the old sailing ship USS Constellation at Newport, Rhode Island, in 1926. The wooden warship, launched in 1854, was used as a training ship.
How is a sailing ship different from a modern one?
Dorothy Norman
Alfred Stieglitz photographed Dorothy Norman, a young photographer and writer who became his close friend. He made many portraits of her in the late 1920s and early 1930s.
Why would a photographer photograph someone again and again?
Composition
Jaromír Funke was a Czech photographer who made abstract pictures from everyday objects in the 1920s. He arranged glass, shadows and light into shapes.
What everyday things can you find in the picture?
Ceremonial Mask Wearer, Nunivak
Edward S. Curtis photographed a man wearing a ceremonial mask in Nunivak, an island off the coast of Alaska, in 1927. The masks were used in dances and stories.
What story would a mask tell?
At Noatak Village
Edward S. Curtis photographed two men in hooded parkas landing their kayaks at the village of Noatak in Alaska in 1927. They had to be dressed for the cold.
How do you stay warm in a kayak?
Ali Fethy Bey
Georges Chevalier photographed Ali Fethi Bey, the ambassador of Turkey, in 1927. Fethi was one of the first prime ministers of the Republic of Turkey.
What does an ambassador do?
Distortograph of Mayor William Hale Thompson
Herbert Ponting invented a machine called a Distortograph that made funny, stretched pictures. This one shows Chicago's Mayor Big Bill Thompson.
What would your face look like in a funhouse mirror?
St. Francis River Flood, Arkansas
This photograph from a flood album shows the St. Francis River near Trumann, Arkansas, during the great Mississippi flood of 1927. Water spread over farms and towns.
What would you do if your house was flooded?
Photographers on a Platform at Lindbergh's Welcome
Photographers stand on a platform above the crowd to take pictures of Charles Lindbergh's welcome in Washington in June 1927. A few weeks earlier he had flown alone across the Atlantic.
Why would everyone want a photograph of Lindbergh?
Crowd on the Washington Monument Grounds to Welcome Lindbergh
Crowds gathered on the Washington Monument grounds on June 11, 1927, to welcome Charles Lindbergh. He had flown nonstop from New York to Paris in the Spirit of St. Louis.
Why was a solo flight across an ocean so amazing?
James Joyce in Paris
Berenice Abbott photographed the Irish writer James Joyce in Paris in 1928. Joyce wrote Ulysses, a famous novel, and he was nearly blind by then.
What would you ask a writer of such a long novel?
Acanthus mollis
Karl Blossfeldt photographed an acanthus plant in 1928 close up, showing the shape of the leaf. He taught art in Berlin and used the pictures to show students how plants make forms.
Which shape in the plant looks like architecture?
Cucurbita
Karl Blossfeldt photographed a plant from the squash family, called Cucurbita, in 1928. He built simple cameras to magnify plants up to 30 times.
How does magnifying a plant change it?
Vogue Fashion Photographs with Model Gurta Andre
Arnold Genthe photographed the model Gurta Andre in 1928 for Vogue. He was a society photographer and made portraits of fashion models.
How are fashion pictures different from portraits?
Victoria Ocampo
Man Ray photographed Victoria Ocampo, an Argentine writer, in 1929 in a dress by Chanel. Ocampo founded a famous literary magazine, Sur.
What would it be like to publish a magazine?
Plant from Urformen der Kunst
This photograph from Karl Blossfeldt's 1928 book Urformen der Kunst, Art Forms in Nature, shows a plant stem magnified. The book became a bestseller and changed how people looked at plants.
What does the plant remind you of?
Otis Steel Mill, Ohio
Margaret Bourke-White photographed the Otis Steel mill in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1929 for Fortune magazine. Her picture of the glowing furnaces made her famous as a photographer of industry.
How can a factory seem dramatic?
Prison Work Crew
Doris Ulmann photographed a prison work crew digging a trench with a guard watching in the South in the 1920s. Prisoners often did road work.
What would working on a crew be like?
Hen and Chickens
Imogen Cunningham photographed a hen and her chicks in 1929. She loved plants and animals, and her sharp, clean pictures were praised.
How do you hold chicks safely?
Leaf Pattern
Imogen Cunningham photographed a leaf pattern in 1929. She made plants look like sculptures by choosing sharp focus and strong light.
What shapes do the veins of leaves make?
Inuk in a Kayak
Edward S. Curtis photographed an Inuit man in a kayak around 1929 at Noatak, Alaska. The kayak is a boat made from skins stretched over a frame.
Why would a boat made from skin be good in cold water?
Crowd with Washington Monument in the Background
Harris and Ewing photographed a crowd at the Washington Monument in 1929. Washington crowds gathered for parades and speeches.
What event do you think the crowd came to see?
Harvesting Sugarcane, Central Romana
Jacob Gayer photographed sugarcane harvesting at Central Romana in the Dominican Republic in 1929. Cane workers cut the tall stalks with machetes.
How would you cut tall stalks of cane?
Derrick Worker on the Empire State Building
Lewis Hine photographed a worker on a derrick high on the Empire State Building in 1930. Hine climbed up with the workers to take his pictures.
Would you work on a skyscraper?
Night View of Manhattan
Berenice Abbott photographed Midtown Manhattan at night from the top of a building around 1930. The glow of lit towers made the city look like a sparkling forest.
What does a city look like from far above at night?
Louis Aragon
Man Ray photographed the French poet Louis Aragon around 1930. Aragon was a founder of the Surrealist movement.
What is surrealism?
Arcady, Where All the Leaves Are Merry
Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed a garden scene in 1930 titled Arcady, after a line of poetry. She was a leading architectural and garden photographer.
Why would someone name a garden Arcady?
Aerial View of the Fremantle War Memorial
Frank Hurley photographed the war memorial in Fremantle, Western Australia, from the air in 1930. He was fond of airplane photographs.
What does a memorial look like from above?
Artichoke, Halved
Edward Weston photographed a halved artichoke in 1930. He found sculptural shapes in vegetables, and the overlapping leaves make graceful patterns.
What shapes do you see inside the artichoke?
Tugboat Frank W. on the Cuyahoga River
Margaret Bourke-White photographed the tugboat Frank W. pulling a boat on the Cuyahoga River in Cleveland in 1929. The river was the center of the city's steel industry.
What does a tugboat do?
Girl Athletes at a Pre-Olympic Night Sports Festival
Girl athletes take part in a night sports festival before the Olympics in 1930. Women's sports were growing quickly.
What sport would you like to try at night?
Railroad Conductor and Engineer
A railroad conductor and an engineer pose beside a train in 1930. The conductor checks tickets and the engineer drives the locomotive.
Who would you rather be?
Family of Nine
The American Red Cross photographed a family of nine sharing a small home in 1930 during the early Depression. Families doubled up during hard times.
How would you share a small room with eight people?
Cabbage Leaf
Edward Weston photographed a cabbage leaf in 1931 and made the wavy edges look like a sculpture. He used a small aperture to get everything sharp.
What does the leaf look like besides a cabbage?
Dualities, Dorothy Norman
Alfred Stieglitz photographed Dorothy Norman in 1932 with a double portrait. His series of her face and hands became a major work.
What can you show with a double photograph?
From My Window at An American Place, Southwest
Alfred Stieglitz photographed the New York skyline from his gallery window, An American Place, in 1932. He photographed the view in all weather for years.
What changes when you look at the same view every day?
Interlude
Pierre Dubreuil made a carefully planned still life from ordinary objects in 1932. It is part of his modernist way of arranging common things.
What ordinary things can you spot?
Cary Grant
Imogen Cunningham photographed the young actor Cary Grant in 1932. She took portraits of celebrities for Vanity Fair.
What makes a movie star look like one?
Ernst Thälmann
Lotte Jacobi photographed Ernst Thälmann, a German Communist leader, around 1932. Jacobi was a German photographer who fled the Nazis.
Why would a photographer have to flee?
American Bobsled Team, Lake Placid
Members of the American bobsled team pose at Lake Placid, New York, in 1932 for the Winter Olympics. Bobsleds race down an icy track.
Would you ride a bobsled?
Betty Robinson Trains for a Comeback
Betty Robinson, the first female Olympic champion in track and field, won the 100-meter dash in 1928. After a plane crash in 1931 she trained to run again.
How does someone recover from a bad injury?
Betty Robinson Runs Again
Betty Robinson discards the crutches she needed after a plane crash. She went on to win a gold medal in the 1936 relay.
What gives someone courage to try again?
Babe Didrikson Zaharias
Mildred Babe Didrikson was a star in track and field, basketball and golf. She won two gold medals and a silver at the 1932 Olympics in Los Angeles, and she later became a champion golfer.
Which sport would you try first?
In Glacier National Park, Montana
Ansel Adams photographed Glacier National Park in Montana for the National Park Service between 1933 and 1942. His crisp black-and-white pictures made the mountains look huge.
How does black-and-white make mountains look strong?
St. Mary's Lake, Glacier National Park
Ansel Adams photographed St. Mary Lake in Glacier National Park in Montana. Dark mountains frame the still, silvery water.
What do the mountains do to the lake?
Two Medicine Lake, Glacier National Park
Ansel Adams photographed Two Medicine Lake in Glacier National Park. The lake lies below sharp peaks in a quiet valley.
What would you hear at a lake in the mountains?
Gertrude Stein
Carl Van Vechten photographed the writer Gertrude Stein in New York in 1934, when she visited the United States on a lecture tour. Stein wore a vest and her hair short.
Why would a lecture tour be exciting?
Gramercy Park, West Side
Berenice Abbott photographed the west side of Gramercy Park in Manhattan in 1935 for her Changing New York project. The old brownstones stand around a private park.
Why is it special to live around a private park?
Mulberry and Prince Streets
Berenice Abbott photographed Mulberry and Prince Streets in Manhattan in 1935 for Changing New York. An old building with a gambrel roof stands among new tenements.
What kinds of buildings do you see?
Fish Market, South Street
Berenice Abbott photographed fish dealers and the Meyers Hotel on South Street in Manhattan in 1935. The old Fulton Fish Market was one of the busiest in the country.
What smells would you notice?
First Avenue and East 70th Street
Berenice Abbott photographed First Avenue and East 70th Street in Manhattan in 1935. Shops and apartments in older buildings line the street.
What changes in a city over time?
Joe Louis
Underwood and Underwood photographed the boxer Joe Louis in 1935, the year he became a national hero. He later held the heavyweight title for nearly twelve years.
What makes a champion?
Children at Play, Washington, D.C.
Carl Mydans photographed children playing in a Washington, D.C., street in 1935 for the Resettlement Administration. The pictures showed daily life during the Depression.
What games do you play outside?
Train Station, Radburn, New Jersey
Carl Mydans photographed the train station at Radburn, New Jersey, a planned community built in the 1920s. Radburn was designed with parks and separate roads for cars and walkers.
Why would a planner separate cars from people?
Dust Storm near Mills, New Mexico
Dorothea Lange photographed a dust storm near Mills, New Mexico, in 1935 for the government. In the 1930s, drought turned the plains into a dust bowl.
What would a dust storm be like?
Cedar Street from William Street
Berenice Abbott photographed Cedar Street in Lower Manhattan in 1936 for Changing New York. Tall buildings line a narrow canyon.
How does a street look at the bottom of skyscrapers?
Broadway and Thomas Street
Berenice Abbott photographed Broadway and Thomas Street from above in 1936 for Changing New York. Looking down shows the traffic and people.
What do you see from high above a street?
Dunes, Oceano
Edward Weston photographed the sand dunes at Oceano, California, in 1936. The curves look like the shapes of bodies, and the light makes strong ridges.
What shapes does the wind make in sand?
Custom House Statue behind the New York Produce Exchange
Berenice Abbott photographed two statues behind the New York Produce Exchange building in 1936. The old buildings in Lower Manhattan were being torn down.
What happens to old statues when a building is torn down?
Burroughs Children Playing in the Yard
Walker Evans photographed the children of the Burroughs family in Hale County, Alabama, in 1936. He was working for Fortune magazine with the writer James Agee, who wrote about tenant farm families.
What games do you play in the yard?
California Migrant Camp
Dorothea Lange photographed a migrant camp in California in 1936. Families who had lost farms in the Dust Bowl lived in tents and cars.
What would you pack if you had to leave home?
Woman Sharecropper near West Memphis, Arkansas
Carl Mydans photographed an African American woman sharecropper near West Memphis, Arkansas, in 1936. Sharecroppers farmed land owned by others and shared the crop with the landlord.
Why was sharecropping a hard life?
Sharecropper's Shack
Carl Mydans photographed a sharecropper's shack near West Memphis, Arkansas, in 1936. The wood house is small and weathered.
What would it be like to live in a place like this?
Opening of the Garment Factory, Hightstown, New Jersey
Carl Mydans photographed the opening of a garment factory in Hightstown, New Jersey, in 1936. It was part of a government plan to move families to a new town called Jersey Homesteads.
What would you make in a factory?
H. S. Wimmer Farm
Carl Mydans photographed a farm in Pennsylvania in 1936 for the Resettlement Administration. The agency studied farms to see how to help farmers.
How would you improve a farm?
Church, South Carolina
Walker Evans photographed a small church in South Carolina in 1936. He loved plain buildings and photographed them straight on.
What do you notice about the church's simple shape?
Church, St. Marys, Georgia
Walker Evans photographed a church in St. Marys, Georgia, in 1936. His clear, straight-on pictures of buildings became a model for later photographers.
How does a straight-on photograph feel?
Sharecropper's Grave, Hale County, Alabama
Walker Evans photographed a simple grave in Hale County, Alabama, in 1936. The grave is marked by a mound of earth and a few objects.
What does a simple grave say about a person?
Kitchen Corner in an Alabama Tenant Farmer's House
Walker Evans photographed a corner of a tenant farmer's kitchen in Alabama in 1936, with shelves and plain dishes. His pictures show poverty and dignity.
What can you learn from a kitchen?
George Gershwin
Carl Van Vechten photographed the composer George Gershwin in 1937. Gershwin wrote Rhapsody in Blue and the opera Porgy and Bess.
What would you do if you wrote music like Rhapsody in Blue?
Frida Kahlo Seated Next to an Agave
Toni Frissell photographed the Mexican painter Frida Kahlo seated beside an agave plant in 1937. Kahlo's self-portraits are famous around the world.
How would you pose with a plant?
Firehouse, Park Avenue and East 135th Street
Berenice Abbott photographed an old wooden firehouse in Harlem in 1937. The little two-story shingled building stood among larger ones.
What would it be like to live in a firehouse?
Francis Townsend Speaking at a Club
Dr. Francis Townsend speaks to a club in 1937. He proposed a pension plan for older Americans during the Great Depression that led to Social Security.
Why is a pension for older people a good idea?
Ringwood Manor Smithy

A photograph for the Historic American Buildings Survey shows the blacksmith shop at Ringwood Manor in New Jersey in 1937. The Survey hired photographers during the Depression to record old buildings.
What would a blacksmith make?
Harpswell Meetinghouse
Josiah Tubby photographed the Harpswell Meetinghouse in Maine in 1937 for the Historic American Buildings Survey. The plain church dates from 1757.
Why would a village have a plain meetinghouse?
Albert Einstein
Lotte Jacobi photographed Albert Einstein in 1937, a few years after he moved to the United States. Einstein gave her several sittings.
What would you ask a great scientist?
Migrant Agricultural Worker near Holtville, California
Dorothea Lange photographed a migrant farm worker near Holtville, California, in 1937. Many workers followed the crops from one place to another.
How would you live if you moved with the harvest?
Migrant Agricultural Workers' Home, California
Dorothea Lange photographed the home of migrant farmworkers in California in 1937, a shack with a patchwork roof. Housing for field workers was poor.
What would you use to patch a roof?
Doorway of the Reverend Ebenezer Gay House, Suffield
Everett Keeler photographed the carved doorway of an 1700s house in Suffield, Connecticut, in 1938. The doorway has a broken pediment, a style typical of colonial homes.
What do you see in the doorway's carving?
Einstein and Infeld Writing a Book
Lotte Jacobi photographed Albert Einstein and Leopold Infeld in 1938 writing The Evolution of Physics. The two scientists wrote a book to explain modern physics to readers.
How would you explain a hard idea?
Surf, China Cove, Point Lobos
Edward Weston photographed the surf at China Cove at Point Lobos, California, in 1938. The waves crash against rocks and curve like ribbons.
How does the water move around the rocks?
Methodist Church, Urbana, Ohio
Ben Shahn photographed a Methodist church in Urbana, Ohio, in 1938 for the Farm Security Administration. A simple white building with a spire sits on a street corner.
Why do small towns often have a church in the middle?
Leaving Church, Linworth, Ohio
Ben Shahn photographed people leaving church in Linworth, Ohio, in 1938. They are in their Sunday best.
What do you wear to special events?
The Thaxton Family, near Mechanicsburg, Ohio
Ben Shahn photographed the Thaxton family near Mechanicsburg, Ohio, in 1938 for the Farm Security Administration. Shahn was also a painter and noticed faces and clothes.
What does the family's clothing tell you?
Main Street, Plain City, Ohio
Ben Shahn photographed the main street of Plain City, Ohio, in 1938. Cars and low brick buildings line the street.
What would you find on a main street in a small town?
Bus Station, Marion, Ohio
Ben Shahn photographed the bus station in Marion, Ohio, in 1938. Buses connected small towns to cities.
What would it be like to wait for a bus then?
Family on Relief, Lancaster, Ohio
Ben Shahn photographed a family on relief in Lancaster, Ohio, in 1938. Relief meant help from the government for families who had no work.
How can a government help families in hard times?
Dinner Time During Wheat Harvest
Ben Shahn photographed workers eating dinner during the wheat harvest in central Ohio in 1938. Neighboring farmers helped each other, and a big meal fed the crew.
What would you cook for harvest workers?
Family in Marysville, Ohio
Ben Shahn photographed a family in Marysville, Ohio, in 1938. His pictures were used by the Farm Security Administration to show how Americans lived.
How can a photograph show how a family lives?
Blowing Dust in the Oklahoma Panhandle
Dorothea Lange photographed blowing dust in the Oklahoma Panhandle in 1938. Clouds of dust covered farms during the Dust Bowl.
What would you do in a dust storm?
Loaders at the Pillsbury Flour Mill, Minneapolis
John Vachon photographed loaders at the Pillsbury flour mill in Minneapolis in 1939. Minneapolis was known as the Mill City because it made so much flour.
How would you move sacks of flour?
Tyrone Power and Annabella After Their Wedding
The Los Angeles Times photographed the film stars Tyrone Power and Annabella after their wedding in Bel Air in April 1939. Movie weddings drew crowds of fans.
Why would people want to see a movie star's wedding?
Migrant Worker in Camp, California
Dorothea Lange photographed a migrant worker in a camp in California in 1939. Families lived in tents and cars near the fields.
What would you miss about home?
Commuters Waiting for the Bus
Jack Delano photographed commuters who had just come off a train and were waiting for a bus in 1939. Commuting to work was part of daily life in New England.
How do you get to school or work?
Railroad Cars and Factory Buildings, Lawrence, Massachusetts
Jack Delano photographed railroad cars and factory buildings in Lawrence, Massachusetts, in 1939. The city was famous for its textile mills.
What were the mills making?
